content.text:
The pattern fits one candidate, NaEu(MoO4)2 (mp-1221078), a scheelite-type phase. I located peak positions by eye-counting points on the 0.05° grid, so they carry about ±0.1–0.2° uncertainty.

**Observed peaks.** The strongest peak is at about 28.6–28.7° (100). Other clear peaks are near 15.25° (~20), 18.3–18.4° (~23), 34.0° (~21) and around 47–48° (~23).

**NaEu(MoO4)2.** Converting the CIF's primitive cell gives a conventional body-centred tetragonal cell of a ≈ 5.29 Å and c ≈ 11.54 Å. Its calculated reflections match the observed peaks:

| Reflection | d (Å) | Calculated 2θ (°) | Observed peak |
|---|---|---|---|
| (002) | 5.77 | 15.35 | ~15.25° |
| (101) | 4.81 | 18.45 | ~18.3–18.4° |
| (112), strongest scheelite line | 3.14 | 28.4 | ~28.6–28.7°, the 100 peak |
| (004) | 2.885 | ≈31.0 | weak peak near 31.0–31.5° |
| (200) | 2.64 | ≈33.9 | ~34.0° |

**ErVO4 rejected.** ErVO4 (mp-18880) is also scheelite-type, but its smaller cell (a ≈ 5.06 Å, c ≈ 11.19 Å) puts (112) near 29.6° and (101) near 19.2°. Both are clearly off the observed peaks.

**No second phase.** The small residual peaks, for example near 41°, are weak and do not clearly require a second phase. I did not check those minor peaks against the other candidates, so a minor second phase is not fully excluded.

{"present": ["mp-1221078"], "confidence": 0.75, "note": "Strongest peak near 28.6 deg plus peaks near 15.3, 18.4 and 34.0 deg match scheelite-type NaEu(MoO4)2 (a~5.29, c~11.54 A); the smaller ErVO4 scheelite cell would shift these to higher angles."}
